Industry News: Avengers: Doomsday final trailer adds more fuel to Steve Rogers fan theory

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (354 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A newly introduced trailer for Avengers: Doomsday is here, and fans are pretty convinced that Steve Rogers is actually Loki.
  • In the new trailer we see a whole lot of Steve Rogers and Peggy Carter back at their home (though we have no idea what time period or universe they live in)...
  • In a recent development, "That was a good speech back there," Steve claims in the clip.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A newly introduced trailer for Avengers: Doomsday is here, and fans are pretty convinced that Steve Rogers is actually Loki.

In the new trailer we see a whole lot of Steve Rogers and Peggy Carter back at their home (though we have no idea what time period or universe they live in)... but the Steve we see outside in the real world walking alongside Thor seems a bit different.

In a recent development, "That was a good speech back there," Steve claims in the clip. Thor replies, "Yours felt a little average by Cap's standards, don't you think?" Steve then smiles, holds up Mjölnir, and says, "This doesn't bother you, does it?" It would most definitely bother Thor if Loki got to use Mjölnir as a weapon, seeing as only the pure of heart (like Steve Rogers) can hold that hammer, and Loki is far from it.

According to recent reports, I wasn't sure if I agreed with this one... but then I remembered the previous trailer when Loki shows up at Steve and Peggy's home and says, "I think I can help you." Does this "help" consist of Loki using his shapeshifter powers to become Steve Rogers for the purpose of saving the world from multiple oncoming incursions? This still doesn't explain how Loki is able to leave his post at the center of the universe holding up Yggdrasil... but I'm sure that'll be explained.

Avengers: Doomsday arrives in US theaters on December 18 and a few days earlier in the UK on December 16. For more on the MCU, check out our guide to the Marvel timeline and how to watch the Marvel movies in order.

It has been revealed that sharon Horgan had a string of British hits (including a couple we'll talk about here), before scoring stated successes with Divorce, Shining Vale, and Bad Sisters. She's quickly rising in the ranks of TV super-producers, the acerbically funny HBO Max rom-com Youth (in which she also stars) being just the latest.

It has been revealed that this earlier series created by and starring Sharon Horgan is a family sitcom that feels far more believable than most, seeing Irish primary school teacher Sharon (Horgan) hooking up with American ad exec Rob (Rob Delaney) over the course of a week, only to discover that she's pregnant once he returns home. They don't really have feelings for each other, but decide to give it a go at being a couple, eventually falling into marriage just before the birth of their child. There are lots of jokes and plenty of acerbic dialogue, but this isn't Married... with Children. Sharon and Rob can be a bit nasty to each other and to their sloppy friend group, but there's also something rather sweet in the show's conviction that having someone to be a mess with can be one of life's great joys. Stream Catastrophe on Prime Video.

Industry observers note that A little more of a high-concept here, but nevertheless an effective show about reimagining yourself in middle age. Younger follows Liza Miller (Sutton Foster), a recently divorced woman in her 40s who finds that age is a barrier to reentering the publishing industry she left years earlier. After a compliment convinces her that she could pass for a younger woman (poor thing), she manages to convince the right people that she's just 26 in order to land an entry-level job. Seven seasons of misadventures ensue, but much of the show revolves around the twisty-turny relationship between Liza and Josh (Nico Tortorella), a tattoo artist in his twenties. Stream Younger on Netflix.

Sources indicate that bridget Everett stars as Sam Miller, who struggles to find her fresh direction after moving back to her hometown to care for her dying sister. (Don't worry: There's plenty of comedy in the drama, and it's not as heavy as it sounds.) She's solidly middle-aged and starting over, kinda—making new friends in a familiar environment where she has to confront the past and the future alike. Luckily, her love of singing—and a community of goofy oddballs—are there to help. It's another story of a person of a certain age, trying to rebuild their life following an upheaval. Stream Somebody Somewhere on HBO Max.

According to recent reports, when all else fails: Start a punk band. This drama from Sally Wainwright (Gentleman Jack) sees five women start a punk band as a lark, just a fun way to kill some time by entering a local talent context. The women realize very rapidly, though, that they're very, very pissed off—about the workplace for women, menopause, a diminished dating pool, caring for aging parents and grown children—all of it tied up in the ways in which we treat women, and particularly middle-aged women. The band is a way to reclaim their voices, which doesn't erase or negate any of their problems nor drama (and there's plenty here), but gives them a platform with which to make some noise about it. Stream Riot Women on Britbox.

More of a traditional sitcom, not that there's anything wrong with that, this one builds a lot of goodwill with the performance of Leanne Morgan, its lead and co-creator (alongside Susan McMartin and Chuck Lorre). She plays the show's lead: a Knoxville, Tennessee wife and mom, who finds herself suddenly single in her 50s after her husband of 33 years leaves her. It's a genial, old-school hang-out show with a phenomenal veteran supporting cast that includes Kristen Johnston, Ryan Stiles, and Tim Daly. Stream Leanne on Netflix.

Michele Buteau, who also co-created the series) stars here as a fashion-forward stylist who'd devoted herself to the wrong guy for way too long. As the series opens, Mavis Beaumont is ready for a fresh start, putting herself and her career first—which does not preclude falling into a number of romantic entanglements. As she says more than once, she's going to take on the fashion world with a "body-positive attitude, cute v-neck, and some lip-gloss." Stream Survival of the Thickest on Netflix.

Certainly the goofiest take here on the idea of starting over in mid-life, this is very much a traditional three-camera sitcom, albeit one with a stacked cast of TV legends. Writer Melanie (Valerie Bertinelli), beautician Joy (Jane Leeves), and soap diva Victoria (Wendie Malick) wind up spending a wild night in Cleveland after a plane to Paris is diverted, discovering in the process that, while they're seen as over-the-hill back in Los Angeles, they're all Ohio 10s—though the sassy caretaker of their house, Elka (Betty White), might not agree. Stream Hot in Cleveland on Paramount+.

Industry observers note that she'a s hair younger than Alex, but Fleabag (she's only ever referred to as "Fleabag") is trying to rebuild her life after a bad breakup, with extremely mixed results. This very dark comedy-drama follows a free-spirited, deeply angry single young woman living in London and sharing her romantic ups and downs via confessional asides to us, the audience. She falls, rather reluctantly, for "The Priest" (Andrew Scott)—while she's a confirmed atheist, and he's obviously not, the show doesn't turn aside from the general messiness of the situation. Phoebe Waller-Bridge won separate Emmys as the star, creator, and writer of the series. Stream Fleabag on Prime Video.

Maisel was one of Prime’s first truly buzzy original series, a comedy-drama from Amy Sherman-Palladino (Gilmore Girls) about the title’s Midge Maisel (Rachel Brosnahan), a long-time New York housewife of the late 1950s who discovers a talent for stand-up comedy. Inspired by the real-life careers of comedians like Totie Fields and Joan Rivers, the show is warm and welcoming, with great performances and dialogue; it also achieves something rare in being a show about comedy that’s actually funny. Stream The Marvelous Mrs. Maisel on Prime Video.

The major life change in this earlier Sharon Horgan hit is a little different: Julia Johnstone's mother had been a big help in taking care of Julia's children, but she's not going to do it anymore, leaving this working mom (Anna Maxwell Martin) to take the full brunt of childcare for the first time (her husband in the picture, but not much use). She joins up with other working moms involved with a local support group, including shallow Amanda (Lucy Punch), star of her own ongoing spin-off. Stream Motherland on Prime Video and Britbox.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Prolific game license revivers SNEG have released a newly introduced version of Soldiers at War, an ancient turn-based tactics game that will remind you strongly of the X-COM/UFO Series, except that it's set during World War 2.
  • It has been revealed that originally developed by Random Games and published by Strategic Simulations, Inc, the game consists of 18 main scenarios spanning D-Day, Monte Cassino and Cherbourg.
  • It has been revealed that "This edition updates Soldiers at War to run smoothly on modern Windows systems, delivering improved compatibility and performance," promises the GOG page (it's also on Steam).

Prolific game license revivers SNEG have released a newly introduced version of Soldiers at War, an ancient turn-based tactics game that will remind you strongly of the X-COM/UFO Series, except that it's set during World War 2. I don't believe they had Chryssalids back then. Pretty sure grandpa never mentioned any Chryssalids.

It has been revealed that originally developed by Random Games and published by Strategic Simulations, Inc, the game consists of 18 main scenarios spanning D-Day, Monte Cassino and Cherbourg. There's a mission editor, too, and some standalone extra skirmishes. In each scrap, you pick eight men to undertake such feats as raiding V2 sites and hijacking disabled tanks, drawing on a pretty dizzying range of individual soldier actions. Your squaddies level up with experience, and you can equip them with flamethrowers and bazookas. Among the key differences from X-COM is that there's no morale system - your men will never defy orders. Nor is there an overarching base/Geoscape layer.

It has been revealed that "This edition updates Soldiers at War to run smoothly on modern Windows systems, delivering improved compatibility and performance," promises the GOG page (it's also on Steam). "The game now supports 1280x720 widescreen resolution, with rendering improvements for smoother drawing." There are cloud saves and Achievements, too, for today's soldier is not content with merely laying down their life for their country. They must also unlock some percentage-based virtual trophies in the process.

I remember Strategic Simulations, Inc mostly for working on two games in the Close Combat series, but they developed and published a shedload of other strategy games and wargames before their eventual parent manufacturer Ubisoft retired the brand in the noughties. As for Random Games – hold the phone, those guys also made the original Warhammer 40,000: Chaos Gate!

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Rocky has returned to the big screen amid the 2026 movie schedule, but not in the way fans of the fictional boxer would’ve likely expected.
  • It has been revealed that as awards season heats up, the cast and creative team behind I Play Rocky have been making the rounds and promoting the movie.
  • So, after he signed off, I noted — we had the discussion [of] should he come on as a producer.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Rocky has returned to the big screen amid the 2026 movie schedule, but not in the way fans of the fictional boxer would’ve likely expected. Sylvester Stallone’s journey to getting the iconic 1976 film made is chronicled in the acclaimed biopic, I Play Rocky, which is helmed by Peter Farrelly. While Stallone had no direct involvement in the movie, he did give it his official stamp of approval to the creative team. However, the beloved actor accidentally sparked some serious drama after the movie was announced, and I was totally unaware of it.

It has been revealed that as awards season heats up, the cast and creative team behind I Play Rocky have been making the rounds and promoting the movie. Farrelly recently took part in a wide-ranging discussion with Deadline as part of its Contenders series and reflected on making his latest flick. During the discussion, the Dumb and Dumber helmer spoke about receiving input from Stallone early on about his approach to his family, including his father, Frank Stallone Sr. Also, Sly and Farrelly agreed on a key detail that led the latter to make a request:.

There’s a funny story. So, after he signed off, I noted — we had the discussion [of] should he come on as a producer. I said, ‘Personally, I think you should not. I think it’s going to hurt you. Because you come across so great [in the film] and, at the end of the movie, if they see ‘executive-produced by Sylvester Stallone’ they’re going to think you shaped it,’ which he didn’t. And he agreed with that, and I said, ‘Just separate yourself a little from this.’.

Honestly, the Oscar-winning filmmaker’s rationale (as shared on X) makes a lot of sense. If Stallone were credited as a producer on the film, which shows him in a mostly positive light, many may be tempted to think he manipulated the narrative. The Rambo star is, of course, no stranger to moviemaking so, given his directing and producing experience, I can see why he’d agree. Despite coming to an accord on Stallone needing to “separate” himself from the production, that apparently led to a serious faux pas on the actor’s part:.

In a recent development, A week later, he’s doing an interview, and a guy says, ‘What do you think about this movie about the making of Rocky?’ And he goes, ‘I know nothing about it.’ And the internet goes crazy…. [People are like,] ‘These motherfuckers, they’re doing this movie without even going to Sylvester Stallone. Frank Stallone is threatening our lives, [Sly’s] brother. And Frank is like, ‘Can you believe these blah blah blah blah blah.’.

The mere thought of getting heat from fans is daunting enough, but receiving heat from a member of the Stallone family is something else entirely. Farrelly went on to say that he later had another chat with the purveyor and lover of the Rocky films, and it went down as follows:.

I called Sylvester [and] I go, ‘What are you doing?!’ He goes, ‘What?’ I stated, ‘You said you knew nothing about it.’ He goes, ‘You said to separate myself.’ [I said,] ‘Not that far.’ And he states, ‘Oh okay, I will remember that going forward.’.

Recent findings suggest that I Thought Rocky And Creed's Major Fight Scene Would Be The End Of I Play Rocky. So What Happened?

Recent findings suggest that while all this drama was due to a simple misunderstanding, it definitely created quite a mess for the filmmaking team. No lasting damage was seemingly done, though, and I’d say that things have been working out for Farrelly and his collaborators. The movie has been well received and gaining considerable buzz in the lead-up to the Oscars. It even received a stamp of approval from Ryan Gosling. As for Stallone, he admitted he was prepared to be “hypercritical” of the film, but he ended up really enjoying the movie as a whole and lead actor Anthony Ippolito’s portrayal of him.

I’d say that’s a generally happy ending to this story in the aftermath of the unintentional drama. Something I appreciate, though, is that Peter Farrelly is far enough removed from the situation that he can joke about it now. What isn’t a laughing matter, though, is the amount of heart that’s present in I Play Rocky, and fans can check out the film in theaters now.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Lawrence Sullivan, better known to the online world as the 'Florida Joker', is in GTA 6.
  • Grand Theft Auto 6's earliest controversy came from its very first official trailer, when Sullivan alleged one of the teaser's similarly tattooed characters was modeled after him.
  • Rockstar seems to have relented to that last request - the vast GTA 6 credits include none other than one Lawrence Sullivan, listed under the 'Local Population' cast, alongside dozens of other names.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lawrence Sullivan, better known to the online world as the 'Florida Joker', is in GTA 6. After accusing Rockstar Games of using his likeness without consent and then demanding a $10m payout, the two parties have seemingly settled their differences.

Grand Theft Auto 6's earliest controversy came from its very first official trailer, when Sullivan alleged one of the teaser's similarly tattooed characters was modeled after him. The former tattoo model, who first went viral because of a mugshot that shared an uncanny resemblance to Batman's Joker, soon called on Rockstar to pay him $2m. His demand quickly shot up to $10m, before he dropped all legal threats and politely asked to officially work with the developer.

Rockstar seems to have relented to that last request - the vast GTA 6 credits include none other than one Lawrence Sullivan, listed under the 'Local Population' cast, alongside dozens of other names.

GTA 6 players wasted no time, and promptly found the suspect first teased way back in that original 2023 trailer. In its quest to parody all parts of modern life under capitalism, GTA 6 lets you doomscroll through a social media app called Snapmatic, which flings an endless number of short-form clips and thirst traps at you. If you're lucky enough, or if you scroll for long enough, you'll find a video of Sullivan's in-game counterpart beating up a fake lookalike. He certainly sounds like Sullivan, too.

According to recent reports, "Two years y'all been talking crazy about me," he wrote under a recent Instagram post. "Who got the last laugh now?!".

The GTA 6 credits were illuminating for other reasons, too. We finally know who voices the game's loveable duo, Jason and Lucia, for one. All 34 of the infamously fired Rockstar workers also appear in GTA 6's credits. The controversial move eventually led to accusations of union busting on Rockstar's part, which is currently being investigated as part of an employment tribunal in Scotland.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Nvidia has reinstated its disgraced former CEO and leather jacket collector Jensen Huang as president, CEO, and director of its board, according to a press release today.

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia back in 1993, was forced to resign from his positions at the firm earlier this month, after it came to light he had an affair with a Chinese businesswoman named Alice Huang, a former executive at Singaporean tech firm Megaspeed International who was suspected by US intelligence of being an asset of the Chinese Ministry of State Security. Huang also reportedly carried out two additional affairs with Nvidia employees.

He was replaced by Nvidia CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO. The Nvidia board initially responded to pressure from tech industry leaders to bring Huang back with a statement that he would not be reinstated. He has now been reinstated.

"Nvidia today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board", confirmed the corporation in a press release. "The Board of Directors voted unanimously to reinstate Mr. Huang following a series of discussions and meetings with Mr. Huang, after which the Board was satisfied with respect to Mr. Huang’s candor and ability to lead Nvidia.

Industry observers note that "In the process of reaching its decision, the Board received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk". Huang has a close relationship with US president Donald Trump, and Trump has backed calls for Huang's reinstatement.

Industry observers note that markets were unhappy with Huang's dismissal earlier this month; when it was announced, Nvidia shed billions of dollars in market value as traders adjusted to the prospect of a future without his leadership. The announcement of his reinstatement has sent Nvidia share prices skyrocketing by over 30%.

"I am honored to return to Nvidia and lead one of the most consequential technology companies in the world at the beginning of a new industrial revolution", said Huang. Meanwhile, Nvidia has formed "a committee comprised solely of independent directors to investigate" Huang's affair with a possible Chinese intelligence asset and says that "investigation will proceed to conclusion.".

You Can Try WhatsApp's New Disappearing Text Messages Early

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (439 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Like Snapchat messages, WhatsApp's "View Once" feature is a great way to send things you don't want living on your friends' devices.
  • As reported by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is now beta testing View Once for text messages, too.
  • As WABetaInfo highlights, the first time you use this feature, WhatsApp will present a pop-up explaining the feature, how "View Once text gives you more privacy," and that when you send the message, it'll disappear from the chat after the recipient opens it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Like Snapchat messages, WhatsApp's "View Once" feature is a great way to send things you don't want living on your friends' devices. You can send voice messages, photos, and videos that will "self-destruct" after they're opened, limiting (if not eliminating) the risk of your friends keeping them forever. However, View Once has a major limitation: While WhatsApp will let you send voice memos and images that way, you can't use it to send texts, meaning every one you send will live on (unless you unsend it yourself).

That's now changing. As reported by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is now beta testing View Once for text messages, too. Soon enough, you'll be able to send voice memos, photos, videos, and texts as one-time-only messages. That way, you can send sensitive information via text—say, a password or an notable account number—without worrying about it persisting. Here's how it works: You craft your text message as you usually do, but rather than tap the send button, you hold it. You'll see the usual "Schedule message" option, but once the feature rolls out, you'll also find a newly introduced "View Once" option as well.

As WABetaInfo highlights, the first time you use this feature, WhatsApp will present a pop-up explaining the feature, how "View Once text gives you more privacy," and that when you send the message, it'll disappear from the chat after the recipient opens it. WhatsApp also explains that recipients cannot share, forward, save, or take screenshots of View Once text messages. Recipients won't see the text appear in the usual chat interface, either; instead, your recipient will need to open the message in a separate window. Once they close this page, the message disappears.

Sources indicate that as mentioned above, this feature is presently in testing, so it's only available to WhatsApp beta testers. What's more, only the Android version of the beta has access at the moment, so iOS beta testers are out of luck. (That said, the WhatsApp iOS beta is perpetually full, so there's not much you could do even if WhatsApp made this test available on iPhone.).

If you have an Android device, you can enroll in the WhatsApp beta to try out "View Once" text messages today. According to WABetaInfo, the feature is live as of WhatsApp version 2.26.45.6. To enroll, open the WhatsApp beta page on the Google Play store and enroll your account in the beta. If you don't have WhatsApp on your phone already, download it here; if you do, reload the page and install the latest update. This will update your existing WhatsApp app to the latest beta version.

Latest Update: After taking seven years to make Persona 6 and four years to make Persona 5, Atlus promises future games will come quicker

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (383 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Eurogamer

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Persona 6 is still slowly chugging in the background, but developer Atlus is promising that future games in its beloved RPG series won't take quite as long as they used to.
  • Industry observers note that there was a four year gap between 2012's Persona 4 Golden and the original Persona 5, and it's already been seven years since the expanded Persona 5 Royal first dropped.
  • According to recent reports, P-Studio general producer Kazuhisa Wada recently assured folks that the pattern wouldn't repeat again.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Persona 6 is still slowly chugging in the background, but developer Atlus is promising that future games in its beloved RPG series won't take quite as long as they used to.

Industry observers note that there was a four year gap between 2012's Persona 4 Golden and the original Persona 5, and it's already been seven years since the expanded Persona 5 Royal first dropped. Despite the sometimes agonising wait filled with countless spin-offs and collaborations with live service games, we've only seen a vague teaser trailer for the next proper Persona.

According to recent reports, P-Studio general producer Kazuhisa Wada recently assured folks that the pattern wouldn't repeat again. "Persona 6 is not the end," he said in a Sega Samania interview translated by GamesRadar. "We have been working to make sure that people won't have to wait as long for the next game as they have previously. In order for Persona to grow as an IP, we consider how to live up to people's expectations in terms of creativity and development every day.".

Wada doesn't go into any more detail about how Atlus plans to release Persona games quicker. Is the next mainline game already in development alongside Persona 6, or is Atlus just streamlining how it makes games? Either way, the studio seems to have abandoned its divisive habit of returning to and improving its games after a few years - P3 Portable, P4 Golden, P5 Royal. I imagine that'll cut down on wait times, at least somewhat.

Sources indicate that "Large-scale RPGs like the Persona series take five years or more to develop," he added. "So there can be a long time between numbered entries.".

As for Persona 6 itself, Wada unsurprisingly "can't say much" about the much-hyped, high-schooling, demon-punching game. "But we want our games to demonstrate all of the hard work we've put in. With that in mind, we are creating something better than anything we've made before, and that is hugely satisfying.".

We don't know much about Atlus' occult sequel, officially, but a massive information leak earlier in the year revealed a full achievement list for Persona 6 and a bunch of other unreleased games, including Kingdom Hearts 4 and an unannounced Sea of Thieves project. Be wary of online spoilers, then.

TinyBuild CEO tells devs not to stress about AI clones "because game feel is impossible to copy"

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (616 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The burgeoning AI takeover that ramped up a few years back has caused a lot of human stress for a lot of different reasons.
  • One way to curb the potential of your game being cloned with AI tools to shorten the time between the game's announcement and release, reckons Alex Nichiporchik, CEO of tinyBuild, the publisher behind the ironically named cyberpunk shopkeeper sim, Probably Stolen.
  • Much more key than market timing, in Nichiporchik's view, is what he calls "game feel." I probably don't need to explain this, but game feel generally refers to how a game feels to play, who woulda thunk?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The burgeoning AI takeover that ramped up a few years back has caused a lot of human stress for a lot of different reasons. Workers across many industries fear for their livelihoods, and on a much more existential scale, there's been substantial debate from industry leaders about whether AI will one day turn hostile and bring about the extinction of the human species, but that's a topic for another publication. For people who make video games, the frightening advancement of AI capabilities means it's easier for nefarious wannabe game developers to take a legitimate game, toss it into an AI prompt, and come out the other side with a legally distinct copycat.

One way to curb the potential of your game being cloned with AI tools to shorten the time between the game's announcement and release, reckons Alex Nichiporchik, CEO of tinyBuild, the publisher behind the ironically named cyberpunk shopkeeper sim, Probably Stolen. Nichiporchik tells GamesIndustry.biz he thinks "the biggest talking point over the next half year is going to be the time to market, and how devs are now afraid of how AI copies their games.".

Much more key than market timing, in Nichiporchik's view, is what he calls "game feel." I probably don't need to explain this, but game feel generally refers to how a game feels to play, who woulda thunk? In other words, it's the tactile sensation of controlling a game on a moment-to-moment level, and it's something generative AI has been shown time and time again to get hideously wrong. Nichiporchik goes a step further and says AI is literally incapable of nailing game feel, and that game developers shouldn't worry about AI clones for that reason.

In a recent development, "Devs should just think about 'How do you make [your game] more difficult to copy?' Because game feel is impossible to copy," he indicates. "You can have all the references and you can have a lot of outsourcing companies trying to copy your game with proper designers, and they still fail. Why? Because of the game feel.

It has been revealed that "As long as you have great game feel and a great game loop, I think you're going to be OK. And the other theory that keeps on confirming itself is time, right? The more time people spend in your game, the more sales you're going to get. So look at your time spent and create great game feel that people love, and everything else is secondary, I think.".

Probably Stolen was announced on August 3 and released on October 28, an unusually brief window between reveal and launch, and Nichiporchik says it's already shifted more than a million units. It seems tinyBuild and developer Questing Goose Studio's success has been undeterred by AI clones unable to flood the market in time, or maybe it's the title's unclonable game feel.

Anthropic CEO reportedly mentioned video games would help pacify the masses who lose their jobs to AI.

  • 9-1-1 has officially wrapped up the first half of its 10th season on the 2026 TV schedule, and it was anything but calm.
  • Buck’s big decision in the Season 9 finale to foster his biological son following the death of his parents has led to some difficulties at the start of Season 10.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Warning! Spoilers ahead for the Season 10 fall finale of 9-1-1, “Et Tu?,” which is available to stream with a Hulu subscription.

9-1-1 has officially wrapped up the first half of its 10th season on the 2026 TV schedule, and it was anything but calm. Thursday’s fall finale included some intense calls, and even more intense scenes between Buck and Eddie as their latest fallout continues. The best friends have not really been on the same page for a while now, and I’ve been worried about them. Luckily, the executive producer is explaining where things stand with them following the midseason finale.

Buck’s big decision in the Season 9 finale to foster his biological son following the death of his parents has led to some difficulties at the start of Season 10. The toddler, Theo, is a bit rambunctious and doesn’t take well to authority. This has put a strain on Buck’s relationship with Eddie, who knows what it’s like to be a single father. It doesn’t help that after Buck decided to give Theo up, Eddie became his foster dad through emergency placement. This has put even more pressure on them, and EP and showrunner Tim Minear told TV Insider why they went in this direction:.

Recent findings suggest that I think conflict is drama, obviously, but it felt… To me, it was sort of an interesting way to have Eddie come in and take Buck’s story away from him in a sense. They both have stories, right? Obviously, Theo is Buck’s biological kid. Buck had every good intention of fostering and growing into that role, which he still has an opportunity to do. But also, I just believe that Eddie would not let that kid go into a group home. And I think there was some truth in what Buck remarked about Eddie’s guilt about being ambivalent about his own son in the first five years of his life.

Sources indicate that buck had donated sperm to his friend and his wife, who were having trouble conceiving a few seasons ago, and after helping her deliver, it didn’t really come up again...until last season. Then, after the couple died in a car crash, Buck felt responsible for the kid and took him in. There was some concern for Buck going into Season 10, and it was obvious this wasn’t going to be easy, especially after seeing Theo’s chaotic energy. So he ultimately believed that Theo would be better with someone else.

However, Minear is right in believing that Eddie, who was the only one who knew what Buck was doing, wouldn’t let Theo go to a group home. Unfortunately, this creates more conflict between them, but it’s what makes the situation more realistic:.

So again, a lot of the stories here this season — look, we’re in Season 10, and a lot of the stories this season are an accumulation of canon that we’ve built up over the past decade with these characters. And that always makes for a richer story, it seems to me. But I actually think Buck and Eddie, conflict is natural, particularly between people who are really close. Nobody can piss you off as much as someone who you’re really close to, and I just think that’s real.

Despite the growing tension in the midseason finale, Buck and Eddie had somewhat made up towards the end of the episode. While Buck wasn’t quite ready to see Theo, he understood why Eddie did what he did. It’s hard to tell where things will go for them in the upcoming year, but with Theo staying with Eddie and Buck coming to terms with everything, it should be interesting. On that note, Minear shares that both of them will have some growing to do for multiple reasons:.

It has been revealed that yeah, I think they’re at an interstitial stage where Buck sees that it is really best for Theo right now to be with Eddie. Maybe neither one of them handled it perfectly, but if they handled it perfectly, then you’d have a five-episode season as opposed to 18. But I think they’re in a good place in their friendship. I think that Theo becomes a spoiler a little bit, and until Buck feels like he can walk into that house and face that kid, there’s kind of a natural barrier there between whatever kind of closeness that he can enjoy with Eddie off the job.

I have been worried about Buck and Eddie’s relationship since the beginning of the season, when it was clear that Buck fostering Theo would bring some problems. And it didn’t get any easier when Eddie became the foster parent. I’m definitely glad that they’ve crossed a barrier, and they both realize how they acted in this situation might not have been the best. However, I am looking forward to seeing what happens now that they have an understanding with each other and Theo.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

9-1-1 is now on its winter hiatus, but the series will return on Thursday, January 7 at 8 p.m. ET on ABC, streaming the next day on Hulu.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Surprise, surprise - GTA 6 is officially the biggest entertainment launch of all time, surpassing its predecessor's 13-year-long record and the already optimistic analyst estimates.
  • Rockstar Games today confirmed that its cultural juggernaut sold a staggering 32.5 million pre-release copies across PS5 and Xbox Series X/S before its official worldwide launch on the 19th of November.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Surprise, surprise - GTA 6 is officially the biggest entertainment launch of all time, surpassing its predecessor's 13-year-long record and the already optimistic analyst estimates.

Rockstar Games today confirmed that its cultural juggernaut sold a staggering 32.5 million pre-release copies across PS5 and Xbox Series X/S before its official worldwide launch on the 19th of November. By the end of its first day on sale, GTA 6 managed to rake in a frankly absurd $3.79bn. Not a bad haul.

As Rockstar was quick to brag, the whopping performance means GTA 6 set "a newly introduced record for entertainment across any medium" by "becoming the biggest entertainment launch in history.".

For context, GTA 5 made around $800m in its opening 24 hours more than a decade ago. That mammoth debut almost looks quaint next to GTA 6's stunning numbers, although it's notable GTA 5 didn't launch immediately in Japan or Brazil - GTA 6 is available in almost every market with access to PlayStation and Xbox consoles.

In a recent development, "It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of Grand Theft Auto VI," remarked Rockstar co-founder and organization president, Sam Houser, in a recent press release. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn't be more excited to share this moment with you.".

Sources indicate that previous estimates guessed that GTA 6 had sold almost 25m copies ($2.5bn in revenue) on day one. It's fair to say the game's staggering performance blew even those sky-high projections out of the water.

According to recent reports, every early indicator pointed to GTA 6's inevitably record-breaking launch. Parent tech giant Take-Two previously stated the game was tracking "well above expectations," as the crime fest sold more pre-orders than any other game in PlayStation Store and Xbox Store history.

Sources indicate that the only question now is whether GTA 6 can ever outsell GTA 5's mammoth 230m copies, which it reached thanks to a very healthy cadence of GTA Online updates. How high GTA 6 can go will likely depend on its multiplayer offering, though Rockstar hasn't said anything concrete about that just yet.

"A game of opposites and awe, minute detail and impossible scale, Rockstar pushes back the horizon of video games once again with GTA 6. An irreducible mix of silliness, intimacy, grand ideas and rock 'n' roll action - and a load more after that," Chris Tapsell gushed in Eurogamer's GTA 6 review.

#154628. I Tested Pangram to See If It Can Really Detect AI-Generated Content Like It Claims

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1031 w)
📖 Baca
AI & Tech ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Lifehacker ↗ Open Full Page

I Tested Pangram to See If It Can Really Detect AI-Generated Content Like It Claims

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1031 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Lifehacker

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that we know it can be difficult for human beings to spot AI-generated content, but can detection software fare any better?
  • Sources indicate that you'll find arguments on both sides of the debate as to whether or not Pangram's claims stand up.
  • Proponents of Pangram would point to an ongoing reward offer—presently at $3,950—available to anyone who can find a pre-2019 (and pre-LLM) piece of writing that Pangram falsely flags as being AI-written.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that we know it can be difficult for human beings to spot AI-generated content, but can detection software fare any better? Pangram is one of the leaders in the field, promising a "near-zero false positive rate" by looking at "subtle cues" in the writing, based on a training and feedback model comparing human-made content with the AI equivalent.

Sources indicate that you'll find arguments on both sides of the debate as to whether or not Pangram's claims stand up. After a short story was flagged by Pangram and then judged to be free from AI, the detection engine has been accused of bias against text from minority writers.

Proponents of Pangram would point to an ongoing reward offer—presently at $3,950—available to anyone who can find a pre-2019 (and pre-LLM) piece of writing that Pangram falsely flags as being AI-written. So far, the reward is unclaimed.

Sources indicate that as the AI detector has recently added AI image and video detection to its capabilities, it seemed a good time to put Pangram's analysis skills to the test for myself. Here's how it performed in the three different content types.

On the human side, I picked out 10 of my most recent articles for Lifehacker, known to be written by a person because I personally wrote them—in the traditional way, I fretted over word choices, went back and changed sentences, and accidentally left in a variety of typos that editors thankfully fixed.

According to recent reports, for the AI content, I rotated between ChatGPT, Gemini, and Claude, and got the LLMs to write 10 articles with the same headlines and the same approximate number of words, for a tech-savvy audience. I even asked the AI apps to vary their language use, so that the output would "read less like an LLM has written it.".

Industry observers note that pangram's AI text detector lets you upload files, but to make the task a little harder, I copied and pasted all of the text into the online article, so it wouldn't be able to rely on any metadata included in the file. The scans got the correct result each and every time: Human-written text came back as 100% human, and AI-written text came back as 100% AI.

According to recent reports, what's more, Pangram was certain about its results. All of the human writing was marked as highly likely to be human, and the vast majority of the AI writing was marked as highly likely to have come from an LLM. There were only a handful of phrases or sentences across thousands of AI words that got a "medium" rather than a "high" ranking for AI.

It has been revealed that now, there have been some edge cases where Pangram has got it wrong—like a poem repeating the same six words thousands of times—but as far as this sample goes, it can't be faulted. Clearly, my writing is too idiosyncratic and too clunky to be confused for the smooth sheen of AI-produced prose.

Industry observers note that to be fair, I do have another advantage over AI: I can actually test out devices and apps in a way that LLM bots can't. ChatGPT can't experiment with One UI 9 (at least not yet), though it can scrape the web for various experiments and tests that real people have done.

However, I was able to fool Pangram to some extent by alternating AI paragraphs with human-written paragraphs. The text was flagged as AI, but the percentage estimate was typically lower (20-25%) than what it actually was (around 50%). If you're offloading some but not all of your writing to AI, some of it might slip though as real.

According to recent reports, image and video detection is the new string to Pangram's bow, so I sifted through my phone's photo and video library for some pieces of content to test the AI on. Again, I used copy and paste to get the files into Pangram rather than uploading them, to limit how much information the AI detector could get from metadata.

In a recent development, again, all the human-made content was recognized as such, with a very high level of certainty—whether it was complicated crowd shots or simpler images of natural scenes. Presumably, there are even more signals to go off than there are with writing, including camera movements, colors, style, consistency, and composition.

Next up, I generated a few images and videos in Google Gemini and ChatGPT, requesting results that would look as photorealistic and "non-AI" as possible—the resulting files covered people, animals, and buildings. As before, I used copy, paste, and a few screengrabs to try and limit the metadata Pangram had access to.

Industry observers note that here, too, the AI identification was spot on, with all of the artificial content recognized as such, to a high level of confidence. This is perhaps not surprising: I think AI images and especially AI video still have more "tells" than AI writing, especially if you've seen a lot of it, so I wasn't expecting Pangram to fail here.

It has been revealed that I did try experimenting with real photos that had a little bit of AI in them, what with tools like Gemini and ChatGPT now so good at image editing, as well as creating pictures from scratch. These were marked as "unsure" by Pangram, though to cut it some slack, only a small amount of the images were altered.

As with the text, the best way to beat Pangram's detection systems seems to be to include some AI embedded in human-made content. It will most likely still fail the "100% human" test, but the tests I ran indicated that Pangram is less certain in these cases, or underestimates the amount of AI there actually is.

Sources indicate that increase the level of AI, and the detection gets more reliable—but if you're only using AI for a small part of whatever it is you're making, it's less worthwhile using AI tools anyway. As far as these tests go, Pangram's claims about accuracy check out, making it a useful tool if you need to ensure something is AI-free.

  • "I can FINALLY share that I play the first-ever nonbinary character in the Grand Theft Auto franchise!" Rose wrote on Instagram.
  • "Absolutely wild to find out THIS was the super-secret game I spent weeks and 17 NDAs filming 3 years ago.".
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6 features the first non-binary character in the series' history, according to actor Jesse James Rose, who plays the role of a museum curator in the game.

"I can FINALLY share that I play the first-ever nonbinary character in the Grand Theft Auto franchise!" Rose wrote on Instagram.

"Absolutely wild to find out THIS was the super-secret game I spent weeks and 17 NDAs filming 3 years ago.".

"I shot this back in my they/them days, and everyone on production ensured I was comfortable and gendered correctly," Rose wrote. The project was kept so secret that Rose wasn't told what it was during filming and only recently learned it was GTA 6.

"GTA was one of the most inclusive & caring sets I've ever been on," they added.

A post shared by Jesse James Rose ✨ (@jamesissmiling).

The role was shot entirely through motion capture, which meant wearing "a unitard made of dots every day". Rose also indicates steps were taken to protect the character in-game: "To mitigate anti-trans violence, I was assured that players would not be able to inflict violence against my character.".

A whole day of the shoot was spent scanning Rose's face, including hours of pulling different expressions. At one point Rose couldn't move a particular muscle, and worried the scan had been ruined, but the director was thrilled.

It has been revealed that "That right there is exactly why we'll never use AI," he said, according to Rose. "A computer could never come up with the face you just made.".

"Remember, in a world consumed with Generative AI, the largest video game in history chose human labour to preserve the integrity of the game," Rose added.

Rose did raise some concerns about pay, though.

"Despite being paid well for my time on set, I'll never see a residual check for my work," Rose wrote, explaining that this is part of SAG’s contract with game developers. As a union leader at one of SAG's sister unions, Rose said there's still "a long way to go to ensure arts workers are fairly compensated for our labour".

Rose also says many other trans people worked on GTA 6, both in front of the camera and behind it. "SO many trans people besides me are featured in GTA VI as other roles, designers, writers, etc... take a note, theatre and TV! We are employable & profitable!!!".

Finally, Rose voiced support for Rockstar's UK staff. "UK-based workers at Rockstar Games are presently voting on whether to unionise, and I sincerely hope their efforts are successful," Rose wrote. "Every arts worker should have a stable job with benefits and fair working conditions protected by a union.".

Industry observers note that GTA 6 is out now on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S. It rolled out on Thursday, although some have been getting in on the action earlier, as a whopping 2m Xbox players in the UK and US took advantage of the trick of changing their console's country. Even Fresh Zealand's tourist board tipped a wink to the sudden influx of virtual 'visitors', telling them "We'd love to have you". It also cheekily offered a video of cheerful tourists admiring the country's resplendent natural beauty. "Life," read the accompanying caption, "because we're getting GTA 6 first.".

Eurogamer called GTA 6 an open world of "awe, minute detail and impossible scale" in our five-star GTA 6 review. And if you need some help getting through the game now it's here, you can check out Eurogamer's Grand Theft Auto 6 walkthrough as well as a breakdown of our Grand Theft Auto 6 cheats.

  • That is in part because the sartorial premise of Bond, the suave British spy, is remarkably simple: Presumably, all it takes to embody 007 is a black tuxedo, a sexy watch, and a pair of well-buffed dress shoes.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There must be no male character across film history who has done more for menswear—and for the suit—than Bond, James Bond.

That is in part because the sartorial premise of Bond, the suave British spy, is remarkably simple: Presumably, all it takes to embody 007 is a black tuxedo, a sexy watch, and a pair of well-buffed dress shoes. And yet, as Daniel Craig, Pierce Brosnan, Sean Connery, and other dangerously handsome men have proven, a mere suit does not a 007 make. This is why, despite Bond being one of the most popular film characters of all time, you will rarely see ordinary men dare to take him on as a Halloween costume. There’s simply more to making Bond than a good tux.

Recent findings suggest that denis Villeneuve is set to direct the next era of the franchise, now under the creative control of Amazon MGM, and Robert Pattinson has been chosen to reincarnate the character conceived by Ian Fleming in 1953. In the announcement clip for Pattinson’s casting, the actor looks the part in a black tuxedo and white shirt, but it’s his eyes, which pierce through the camera rather than down the barrel of his gun, that do most of the talking and offer a suggestion of what Pattinson’s Bond may have to offer. Will he be a little darker and tortured, like his take on Batman? Or perhaps his Bond will be louche and somewhat pricklier.

In a recent development, A safer bet to make is that he will look good. One of the most enduring legacies of the James Bond franchise is how stylish both the character of Bond and the universe built around him have always been. Bond has appeared classic and timeless in style during each of the franchise’s eras, but hindsight offers a much richer perspective.

Pierce Brosnan, The World Is Not Enough, 1999.

Daniel Craig, Casino Royale, 2006.

Recent findings suggest that as portrayed through the decades in the property’s famous title sequence, Bond is a silhouette—a classic, timeless silhouette. Fleming established the look in his development of the character when he made the suit his primary uniform. But it is Terence Young, the director of the first 007 films, who is responsible for the visual definition of Bond.

When Connery was cast as Bond for the first film, Dr. No (1962), Young, an avid wearer of suits himself, took him to his own tailor, Anthony Sinclair. We can credit Sinclair with developing the original silver screen Bond look: The suit was lighter in fit and tailoring than most other English suits at the time. The Bond suit had a soft shoulder and waist, but a strong, wide chest and a low button stance that elongated its wearer. Every Bond suit that’s followed has been measured to the standard of Sinclair’s work, and every Bond actor has had to compete with Connery’s charisma while wearing it.

Roger Moore, The Spy Who Loved Me, 1977.

Brosnan and his Brioni suits were indicative of the 1990s corporate look of the time. Craig wore Brioni too, but only for Casino Royale; Tom Ford created his subsequent suiting, which often stood out for the slim fit popular in the 2010s. Most memorable sartorially is Roger Moore’s take through the ’70s and ’80s, which often deviated from the sleekness that had come to define Bond by creating a little frisson with lighter, brighter fabrics and a bolder sense of playfulness.

Recent findings suggest that the character of Bond, and the actor personifying him at a given time, have also become representative of a certain male standard: Connery in the ’60s, tan and athletic, or Brosnan in the ’90s, polished with lithe elegance. And then came Craig, whose casting was met with skepticism, to put it lightly. His arrival was marked by the image of the actor walking out of the ocean in tight swim trunks in Casino Royale. His strong legs, rounded shoulders, and sculpted, hairless chest cemented then and there the idea of what a leading man had become and would look like for the next two decades.

Daniel Craig as James Bond, Casino Royale, 2006.

Also synonymous with Bond are his watch and many vehicles. Most recently, Bond cars have all been made by Aston Martin, though Brosnan drove some spectacular BMWs. The official Bond timepiece since Brosnan’s turn has been Omega. But before such kinds of commercial partnerships were commonplace in Hollywood, Connery wore watches by Rolex, Gruen, and Breitling, while Moore wore pieces by Seiko.

With the news that Pattinson is taking on the mantle, an equally pressing question emerges: Who will be the first fresh Bond girl?

Some of the most memorable moments in the franchise’s history have been anchored by women. Halle Berry’s emergence from the ocean in an orange bikini and a white belt safekeeping a knife was only made better by the fact that this moment was an homage to the first Bond girl, Ursula Andress, and her ivory two-piece featuring a belt for her own weapon. Then there was Eva Green as Vesper Lynd in a slinky Versace dress in Casino Royale. But it didn’t get better than Grace Jones in A View to a Kill. As May Day, a fabulous femme fatale, Jones wore costumes designed for her by Azzedine Alaïa. How could anyone measure up?

Halle Berry and Pierce Brosnan, Die Another Day, 2002.

Roger Moore and Grace Jones, 1985, A View To a Kill, 1985.

Recent findings suggest that of course, we will have to see how stylistic choices play out in the 26th Bond film, which, like Bond movies of the past, will become emblematic of the era in which we live. It will also, as a creative project, have to contend with the way Hollywood operates today. The fact that Amazon now has full creative control over the franchise—the company acquired MGM, a co-owner of the Bond franchise rights, for $8.45 billion in 2022 and later struck a deal with the other co-owners in regard to creative authority—is the primary indication of that.

Pattinson will also be the first Bond with airtight fashion-brand deals. Craig was an Omega ambassador as an extension of his role as Bond, which made him a household name, and the 007s who came before him operated within a film industry that was not as closely connected to fashion.

Industry observers note that also unlike his predecessors, Pattinson is stepping into the role as a bona fide movie star who has appeared in three other major franchises (Harry Potter, Twilight, and Batman). He’s already one of the most prolific and bankable stars of his generation, and an undeniable part of being a movie star today is becoming the face of a franchise, a brand, or a product.

In a recent development, in September, Pattinson was announced as a global ambassador for Jaeger-LeCoultre, a Swiss watchmaker. But 007 has worn Omega watches onscreen for decades, a partnership between the brand and the franchise that dates back to the Brosnan years. If Omega’s partnership with the franchise remains for this newly introduced installment, it could present a potential conflict if Pattinson’s contract with Jaeger stipulates that he is not allowed to wear another brand’s watch onscreen or front related campaigns for competitors. It may sound like a banal preoccupation, as Pattinson has only just been cast, but there are millions of dollars at play, and actors today often make as much money from brand deals as they do from their turns onscreen.

According to recent reports, pattinson has also been an ambassador for Dior since 2013, serving first as a fragrance ambassador and subsequently as a face for ready-to-wear Dior Homme; he was originally tapped under Kris Van Assche, with his ambassadorship extending through Kim Jones’s tenure at the renamed Dior Men and now continuing with Jonathan Anderson at the helm of the French mega-brand. Will Anderson be providing his suits? The Irish designer has costumed films before, working with Luca Guadagnino on Challengers, Queer, and the upcoming Artificial. To design for the significant screen would hardly be a stretch for him.

It has been revealed that the real question is more existential: Should Bond wear high fashion? To return to the idea of the 007 silhouette, that in itself is counterintuitive to Pattinson saving the world in one of Anderson’s menswear takes on the famous Dior Bar jacket, with its nipped waist and slightly flared hem. And yet in this brave fresh world of brand deals, anything is possible.

I recently switched from Apple Music to Tidal, and I'm happy I made the change. The main reason is AI-made music: Tidal has stricter AI filtering than any other major streamer. The second reason is audio quality. While all major music streaming services do basically the same thing, Tidal's focus has always been on streaming music at the highest possible quality. While other streaming services have more or less "caught up" in terms of pure sonic fidelity, Tidal still is better at getting that quality to your speakers, if you know a few tricks.

Download your playlist as a .txt file. You can do this directly from Apple Music under File>Library>Export Playlist. You can't from Spotify, but the free site Exportify will download any of your playlists as a spreadsheet file you can save.

Industry observers note that install Python on your system. Double click "install certificates" in the folder that opens after installation.

Industry observers note that download this script. Save it in the same file as your playlist.

Recent findings suggest that run the script: (For Mac, open Terminal. For Windows, go to the Command prompt. Type python3 on a Mac or py on Windows.) Drag the script into the terminal window and press enter. It should ask you to drag your downloaded playlist into the window next.

Sources indicate that sign in to Tidal. Hit "Approve" to give permission for Tidal to run the script.

Recent findings suggest that have a banana. The script is going to search for all the songs on your playlist and match them to Tidal's library, so it can take a little while. I tested it with a playlist from Apple Music with 2,397 songs. It took about 20 minutes and found 2,362 of my tracks, a 99% success rate.

Fix the leftovers: The program creates two separate text files for "orphans." One is songs it couldn't find and one is songs it might be worth double-checking manually.

If everything goes well, your large playlist should be available on Tidal.

Note: The script uses a community-created library to talk to Tidal, so it could stop working if Tidal changes things up.

It has been revealed that like most streaming services, Tidal has a "heart" button called "add to my collection." You can click on any track, album, or playlist to "like" and saved it. But Tidal also has a separate, somewhat mysterious "Save for Later" option that puts songs, albums, and playlists into a separate collection. There are a couple reasons for this. First, it keeps a running list of newly introduced-to-you music waiting for you on a rainy day, and secondly, it (presumably) affects your recommendation algorithm differently. While Tidal isn't open about every detail of its recommendation algorithm, I assume "save for later" has less weight (if any) on your future recommendations than "add to my collection.".

Sources indicate that on Tidal, tracks that are 100% AI-generated get an "AI" badge, earn no royalties, and are never placed on a Tidal-curated playlist. Consumers can flip a switch in Settings to either allow or disallow AI content, too. Simple, but there's a bit of nuance that goes beyond the on/off switch. You have to set the AI-toggle separately on each device you use Tidal on, even if it's the same account. I guess this is so I can listen to AI music in my car but not at my desk? Sadly, AI detection is not a science, so some AI-made, and partly AI-made, tracks may still get through.

If you're streaming music from a music app through Bluetooth, the output is automatically compressed to a lower quality, and your phone stays in charge, so a phone call or a notification can interrupt your music. But Tidal's Tidal Connect feature skips the middleman. Music streams directly from your wifi to your speaker and your phone becomes a remote control, so you can take a call, go for a walk, and even run out of phone battery and the music will keep playing.

Have an external device with Tidal Connect compatibility.

Make sure your speaker or other output device and phone or computer are on the same wifi network.

Pick your speaker on your wifi network.

Click the icon again to switch back to your phone.

Plenty of wifi speakers don’t support Tidal Connect, so check before you buy. Tidal keeps the full list of supported devices on its site. There's everything there from WiiM Mini—a $99 small box that adds Tidal Connect to speakers you already own—to dCS components that cost more than a car.

Industry observers note that tidal Connect isn't the only way to get the highest quality audio from Tidal. You can go for an old school, wired path like I have. I play audio from my desktop and route it directly to a mixer via USB. Here's the set-up:.

Settings > Streaming > Audio Quality: Max.

Sound Output: choose your mixer as the output device instead of your computer’s speakers.

It has been revealed that exclusive Mode: On. It’s under Sound Output > More Settings. Tidal sends audio straight to the mixer at each track’s native sample rate, without your computer resampling it or mixing in system sounds.

Force Volume. It's in the desktop app next to Exclusive Mode, under Settings > Streaming > Sound Output > More Settings. Force Volume means Tidal will always output at the highest volume. You'll be controlling the actual volume from your mixer.

Set your levels with the mixer’s faders.

To check what your mixer can handle, look at its maximum sample rate:.

According to recent reports, mac: Open Audio MIDI Setup (in Applications > Utilities), click your mixer, and open the Format menu. The highest number listed is your ceiling.

Windows: Go to Settings > System > Sound, click your mixer, and look under Output settings > Format.

My cheap-ass mixer tops out a 16-bit/48kHz which is CD quality, but not Tidal's top of 24-bit/192kHz, but at least I can control the EQ. Speaking of...

Industry observers note that it's much cooler to turn dials than mess with computer settings. Tidal doesn’t have an equalizer, so if you’re using Tidal Connect or a wired connection, you'll need something to shape the sound. Here are some options:.

According to recent reports, your computer: System-wide EQ apps, like Equalizer APO on Windows or SoundSource on Mac, can adjust Tidal’s output. They don’t work with Tidal Connect though, which bypasses your computer’s audio processing.

Your speaker’s app: If you use a Tidal Connect speaker or streamer, it probably has a companion app for EQ.

A mixer or audio interface: Channel EQ knobs let you adjust bass, mids, and treble by hand, in real time.

Your speakers: Many powered speakers and studio monitors have low and high controls on the back.

A stereo receiver or amp: Old-school bass and treble knobs still work in 2026.

In a recent development, most of Tidal's catalog streams as "better-than-CD quality" FLAC files at every subscription tier, so you might be inclined to click "play music at highest quality on everything." but settings are only as good as the gear you're using, and there are times when lower quality is the right choice. Here's when to turn down the settings:.

When you're in your car: CarPlay and Bluetooth cut audio down to CD quality or less before it reaches your speaker, and with road noises, it usually doesn't matter anyway, so turn the streaming down to "High" instead of "Max." Or download your playlist before you leave, if you must have "as good as possible" audio.

Sources indicate that you have a data cap and are off wifi. Top quality audio requires huge file transfer, so set your mobile data to High or Low and save Max for wifi.

Your connection is spotty: To avoid buffering, a lower setting keeps the music playing.

This isn't a universal hack, but some Android phones have microSD card slots, which can save you a lot of hassle if you're downloading a lot of audio files—an album at high quality might top 1GB, so having an external source will save you a ton of hassle. If your phone has a microSD card slot, go to Tidal's settings, find "download destination" and choose the memory card.

#154614. Pedro Almodóvar Didn’t Think He Could Write a Novel. But Once He Started, the “Story Began to Pour Out”
