📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

GTA 6's first chapter is a lengthy prologue that gets you up to speed on the gameplay, the characters, and the storyline. But once you've cleared the final mission and you start Chapter 2, that's when the game really begins. This is where the protagonists Jason and Lucia cement their decision to go full Bonnie and Clyde, and since this chapter unfolds at a faster pace, you'll want to keep an eye out for a few missable items, people, and missions before you hit the point of no return that leads directly into Chapter 3. Which mission ends Chapter 2 in GTA 6? Appropriately, Chapter 2 in GTA 6 ends with the mission Checking Out after you reach the Move to Vice City point on your map, as Jason and Lucia will leave their current residence behind as they embark on a latest journey to Vice City. To get there, you'll need to complete the following missions: What's in the Bag? Ambulance Chaser Just Moved In Girls' Trip Moses Daily Driver Slam Dunk Breakfast Run Coffee Break Afternoon Delight Checking Out Optional missions There's also a bunch of optional missions you can engage in, in case you want to score some more gear, unlockables, and cash before your Vice City trip: Check Out McKittrick Farm Collect Chemicals for Kyle Hit Avery Pawn Hit Kingpin Bowling Impounded Vehicle Pick Up a Gun Thrillbillies Twist Wrist, Smash, Grab Veteran Hunted (Jason only) Pay your room rent as quickly as possible One of your primary goals in Chapter 2 should be settling your debt with the motel manager Linda, as the more you delay paying her, the higher your checkout fee will be. If you purchased a necklace for Lucia in Chapter 1, Linda will hold it as collateral until the debt is settled, so reclaiming that sentimental piece of jewelry should be a priority. Talk to Wyman Chatting to Wyman and helping him out with his truck will also earn you an invite for a bit of off-roading fun with two of the missions: Thrillbillies and Twist, Wrist, Smash, and Grab. Find missing people While you don't have to tackle the Gellhorn’s Missing Tourist challenge as part of GTA 6's missing people questline during Chapter 2, it is recommended that you get this out of the way early. Starting this quest from Chapter 3 will be more challenging--for spoiler-specific reasons--and you can find those people of interest by checking nearby bulletin boards, posts, and notices. Play some pool Before you rob Frankie's Delights, go shoot a few rounds of pool to check off another task in your quest to be the biggest pool shark around. Grab some collectibles Several collectibles can be found in the Chapter 2 motel, so before you say goodbye to that location for good, grab 'em and sell 'em to help you reach a 100% completion rate in the game. Collectible cards Bryson Powers: On top of the washing machine in the motel laundry room Vicki: In the motel reception bathroom, on the floor underneath the toilet Victor Maravella: Check the fridge in the motel cafeteria Magazines Help Me Help You Help Me: On the motel reception desk Wizard Wang: In the motel cafeteria, next to the radio For more on GTA 6, from completing side missions to finding a tricky location on the sprawling map of Leonida, we’ve got you covered with our Grand Theft Auto 6 guides hub.

According to recent reports, that’s why the PhoneBack by Süti immediately caught my eye. Rather than wrapping my iPhone 18 Pro in a silicone or polycarbonate shell that adds bulks to its size, it’s a minimalist magnetic backplate that protects the rear — while also sprinkling a little of style at the same time. For someone like me who refuses to go caseless, it’s easily the closest alternative I’d be willing to go to achieve that naked iPhone look. Here’s why.

In a recent development, do you hate bulky cases? Well, the Süti PhoneBack is one of the easiest, most efforless iPhone cases around since it snaps onto the back via MagSafe to protect the back glass and camera bump. At just 2.34 mm thin, it adds welcome grip and lets you swap styles, all without adhesives or blocking wireless charging.

What I really love about the PhoneBack is how clever it is at delivering just enough protection against everyday wear and tear, all while completely preserving the "naked" look and feel of the iPhone 18 Pro. Since it relies on a MagSafe connection, it takes seconds to snap directly onto the back — and it beats having to deal with the headaches of installing one of those adhesive vinyl skins.

Best of all, the PhoneBack by Süti gives me a quick and effortless way to change the colors or textures whenever the mood strikes, unlike a permanent wrap that’s notoriously difficult to peel off.

It has been revealed that options range from soft-touch Silicone that I feel is more scratch-resistant, the two-tone look of the iCandy cases, to my favorite NanoLeather one that adds texture to the back of my iPhone 18 Pro. One of the downsides of upgrading from the iPhone 17 Pro to the 18 Pro is that the former’s signature Cosmic Orange color isn’t available, but I’m able to easily emulate that look with the orange silicone PhoneBack.

In a recent development, even though the Süti PhoneBack uses magnets to snap onto my iPhone, it doesn't get in the way of wireless charging at all. That’s because it packs a neodymium magnet array, which still lets me drop the phone right onto a MagSafe or Qi2 charging pad without ever pulling the backplate off. On top of that, I can keep using my favorite MagSafe accessories — like magnetic wallets, desk stands, car mounts, power banks, and more.

It has been revealed that I’ll say it again: the Süti PhoneBack is hands down the closest I’ll ever get to rocking a naked iPhone 18 Pro. It strikes that balance I want with its minimalist design, extra grip, and effortless customization — all without sacrificing MagSafe charging or accessory support. That remarked, I still have to be very careful because it leaves the sides and front glass completely exposed. If you want full 360-degree drop protection, stick with a traditional case. But if you crave that bare-metal feel in hand and just want scratch protection and a fresh look for the back, the PhoneBack is tough to beat.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Grand Theft Auto 6's success continues to come into focus, as a new report from Alinea Analytics says the game sold 44.9 million copies through its first weekend. This would be up from the 32.5 million copies that Rockstar owner Take-Two announced last week, covering the game's pre-purchases alone. According to Rhys Elliott of Alinea Analytics, GTA 6 has reached 33.7 million copies sold on PS5 and 11.2 million on Xbox Series X|S, for a split of 75.1% to 24.9%. Take-Two announced $3.79 billion in sales for GTA 6 on day one, and Alinea estimated that the figure has grown to $4 billion through its first four days. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1YEHOKYVTho Sony and Microsoft keep 30% of the revenue for digital copies via platform fees, so those companies are winners here as well. Elliott went on to point out that GTA 6's $4 billion in revenue thus far is roughly equal to the combined box office results for this year's two biggest movies, Spider-Man: Brand New Day ($2.5 billion) and The Odyssey ($1.8 billion). Of course, GTA 6 is an $80-$100 game, while (hopefully) no one is spending that much to see a movie, at least not at one time. Elliott also shared data that reveals around 40.8 million people logged in to play GTA 6 on Sunday, November 22, with PS5 making up 76% of those players. Additionally, Elliott noted the data shows that about 20% of players--or about 9 million people--have spent more than 20 hours in the game already. GTA 6 is only going to get bigger when it comes to sales as more and more people buy the game. Additionally, GTA 6 is expected to come to PC in 2027, which will be another selling cycle for the game. Beyond this, GTA 6 is expected to add an online mode in 2027 that will no doubt feature microtransactions and other ways for Rockstar to make money off the fanbase. For more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first. And if you’re eager for news on GTA 7? Get comfortable, because Rockstar is not going to announce it anytime soon.

Take-Two unveiled $3.79 billion in sales for GTA 6 on day one, and Alinea estimated that the figure has grown to $4 billion through its first four days.

Industry observers note that elliott went on to point out that GTA 6's $4 billion in revenue thus far is roughly equal to the combined box office results for this year's two biggest movies, Spider-Man: Brand New Day ($2.5 billion) and The Odyssey ($1.8 billion). Of course, GTA 6 is an $80-$100 game, while (hopefully) no one is spending that much to see a movie, at least not at one time.

Elliott also shared data that shows around 40.8 million people logged in to play GTA 6 on Sunday, November 22, with PS5 making up 76% of those players. Additionally, Elliott said the data shows that about 20% of players--or about 9 million people--have spent more than 20 hours in the game already.

According to recent reports, GTA 6 is only going to get bigger when it comes to sales as more and more people buy the game. Additionally, GTA 6 is expected to come to PC in 2027, which will be another selling cycle for the game. Beyond this, GTA 6 is expected to add an online mode in 2027 that will no doubt feature microtransactions and other ways for Rockstar to make money off the fanbase.

According to recent reports, for more, check out GameSpot’s GTA 6 review and our rundown of the five best things to do first. And if you’re eager for news on GTA 7? Get comfortable, because Rockstar is not going to announce it anytime soon.

From a gown purchased with wartime rations to a secret engraving on the ring: Inside the historic royal wedding of Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip married in 1947, going on to make history by achieving the longest marriage of any British sovereign couple.
  • November 2, 1947: Queen Elizabeth—then Princess Elizabeth—with Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, King George VI and Queen Elizabeth (right) and members of the immediate and extended Royal Family at Buckingham Palace after their wedding.
  • The Queen and Prince Philip’s love story began back in 1939.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip married in 1947, going on to make history by achieving the longest marriage of any British sovereign couple. Back then they were, of course, Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip of Greece and Denmark, tying the knot in the rather austere years of post-war Britain. So, what really happened on their wedding day?

November 2, 1947: Queen Elizabeth—then Princess Elizabeth—with Prince Philip, Duke of Edinburgh, King George VI and Queen Elizabeth (right) and members of the immediate and extended Royal Family at Buckingham Palace after their wedding.

The Queen and Prince Philip’s love story began back in 1939. Princess Elizabeth was just 13 years old; her dashing distant cousin, Prince Philip of Greece and Denmark, was five years her senior and about to join the Royal Navy. They met as she toured the Royal Naval College at Dartmouth; he was the young officer assigned to escort her around that day.

Determined to marry for love, Elizabeth was stated to be rather taken with Philip, who was described at the time as ‘handsome as any film star.’ The pair were soon writing letters to each other, and later, occasional chaperoned meetings took place.

The couple on their engagement, 1947.

In 1946 Philip proposed in Scotland, and she immediately remarked yes. However, her father, King George, reportedly insisted the couple resist announcing their engagement until the Princess, who was just 20, was a little older. In the end, her parents gave in to her wishes, and Philip officially proposed to Princess Elizabeth in 1947, with a three-carat diamond ring he designed using stones taken from a family tiara that belonged to his mother, Princess Alice of Battenberg. It was created by London jeweller Philip Antrobus Ltd.

Princess Elizabeth with Philip Mountbatten on their wedding day.

The Royal Family were adamant that the wedding of Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip would reflect the country’s post-war situation while also offering a chance for the nation to celebrate.

Industry observers note that like many brides at the time, Princess Elizabeth had to save her rationing coupons to buy the materials for her dress but was given an extra 200 from the government to help. While well-wishers generously sent their own to the royal, they had to be sent back as rules dictated that coupons could not be shared outside of households.

Industry observers note that designed by Norman Hartnell, Princess Elizabeth’s wedding dress was made from ivory silk, duchesse satin and silver thread; the dress featured crystals, 10,000 seed pearls, a fitted bodice, heart-shaped neckline, long sleeves and a 15-foot train. It was made in just seven weeks by 350 skilled women since the wedding took place only four months after the couple’s engagement announcement. Norman Hartnell also designed Elizabeth’s going-away outfit.

Industry observers note that princess Elizabeth’s wedding day tiara was called the Queen Mary Fringe Tiara. It had belonged to her grandmother, Queen Mary, and had been given to her as a wedding present in 1893. It was remade from a tiara/necklace that Queen Victoria had bought from Collingwood and Co.

As Elizabeth was getting ready on the morning of the wedding, it snapped. Luckily, royal jeweler Garrard was apparently on hand to fix it, and the Queen later revealed, “I think he taped up the spring.”.

In a recent development, princess Elizabeth’s other wedding day jewelry included two pearl necklaces. The shorter of the two necklaces was the “Queen Anne” necklace, stated to have belonged to Anne, the last Stuart Queen. The other was known as the “Queen Caroline,” and is said to have belonged to the wife of King George II. Both necklaces were left to the Crown by Queen Victoria and were given to Elizabeth as a wedding present by her father.

In a recent development, all royal bridal bouquets contain myrtle from a myrtle bush planted by Queen Victoria at Osborne House. Princess Elizabeth’s also had white orchids and was laid on the grave of the Unknown Warrior at Westminster Abbey the day after the wedding.

There were eight bridesmaids at Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip’s wedding: Princess Margaret, Princess Alexandra, Lady Pamela Mountbatten, Diana Bowes-Lyon, Lady Elizabeth Lambart, Margaret Elphinstone, Lady Caroline Montagu-Douglas-Scott, and Lady Mary Cambridge.

Her two pages were Prince William of Gloucester and Prince Michael of Kent, both aged five at the time.

The bridesmaids were given silver Art Deco-style compacts with the couple's initials and a crown engraved on the lid, set with five cabochon sapphires.

The Duke of Edinburgh's best man was David Mountbatten, the Marquess of Milford Haven.

Knowing that Elizabeth hated cigarettes, Prince Philip reportedly gave up smoking on the morning of his wedding “suddenly and apparently without difficulty,” according to his valet, John Dean.

The wedding took place at Westminster Abbey on November, 20th, 1947 at 11:30 a.m. Princess Elizabeth was the 10th member of the Royal Family to be married at Westminster Abbey.

Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip walking down the aisle of Westminster Abbey, followed by their bridesmaids and pages.

There were 2,000 guests in attendance, including the likes of the King of Iraq, Princess Juliana and Prince Bernhard of the Netherlands and the Hereditary Grand Duke of Luxembourg and Princess Elisabeth of Luxembourg. The ceremony was broadcast on the radio to millions of listeners.

Together with her father, Princess Elizabeth left Buckingham Palace in the Irish State Coach. (In her later years, it had been Queen Victoria’s state carriage of choice, as she declined to use the Gold State Coach following the death of Prince Albert.).

The wedding ceremony was officiated by the Archbishop of Canterbury, Geoffrey Fisher, and the Archbishop of York, Cyril Garbett.

The organist and Master of the Choristers at the Abbey, Australian William Neil McKie, was the director of music for the wedding and there were 91 singers; the abbey choir was joined by the choirs of the Chapel Royal and St George's Chapel in Windsor.

The service started with a specially composed fanfare by Arnold Bax and finished with Felix Mendelssohn's “Wedding March,” with ceremony hymns including “Praise, my Soul, the King of Heaven” and “The Lord's my Shepherd.”.

The bride and groom knelt on orange boxes covered in pink silk at the altar as a nod to post-war austerity.

On the day of the wedding, Philip was given the title of Duke of Edinburgh by his father-in-law, King George VI. After the Queen ascended the throne in 1953, she made the decision in 1957 to make Philip a prince of the UK, in addition to his dukedom.

The wedding rings were made from a nugget of Welsh gold which came from the Clogau St David's mine, near Dolgellau.

According to Royal biographer Ingrid Seward, who wrote Prince Philip: Revealed, Philip had a secret message inscribed inside his wife's wedding band, a message that only the engraver, Queen Elizabeth, and her husband knew the contents of.

After the service, a wedding breakfast was held in the Ball-Supper Room at Buckingham Palace for 150 guests only, with Filet de Sole Mountbatten, Perdreau en Casserole and Bombe Glacée Princess Elizabeth on the menu.

During the breakfast, the string band of the Grenadier Guards played music while guests were greeted with individual posies of myrtle and white Balmoral on their place settings as the wedding favors.

The couple waving from the balcony of Buckingham Palace.

Famously, the newlyweds went onto the balcony at Buckingham Palace to wave to the huge crowds on the Mall.

Although the royal couple received 11 wedding cakes, the official traditional fruit cake was baked by McVitie and Price and was four tiers and nine feet high. The wedding cake was decorated with both coats of arms, including the monograms of the bride and groom, sugar-iced figures of their favorite activities, and regimental and naval badges.

Mr Schur, chief confectioner at McVitie and Price, putting the final touches to the wedding cake.

The newlyweds cut the cake using the Duke's Mountbatten sword, which was a wedding present from the King.

It has been revealed that over 10,000 people sent telegrams congratulating Elizabeth and Philip, and around 2,500 wedding presents were sent from around the world. These included a cloth from Mahatma Gandhi that he’d woven himself, which Queen Mary mistook for an “indelicate” loincloth.

After their wedding breakfast, Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip headed to Waterloo station, joined by Elizabeth’s corgi, Susan, catching a train to Hampshire to spend their wedding night in Broadlands, the home of Philip's uncle, Earl Mountbatten.

The rest of their royal honeymoon was spent at Birkhall on the Balmoral Estate in Scotland.

Princess Elizabeth and Prince Philip being showered with rose petals as they leave Buckingham Palace, London, for their honeymoon.

That day can't arrive soon enough for Marvel Studios, which, aside from "Deadpool & Wolverine," has been knocking out box office disappointments relative to their budgets. Advance ticket sales indicate that "Doomsday" is going to open huge at the box office, so, if nothing else, Marvel and parent firm Disney will be pleased.

Industry observers note that but will the movie be any good? After all, quality has also been a problem for Marvel lately. Then again, 2026 has been considerably stronger for the Marvel Cinematic Universe on that front thanks to "Spider Man: Brand Fresh Day" and the streaming series "Wonder Men" and "VisionQuest." So, hopefully, directors Joe and Anthony Russo will build on these successes by delivering a thrilling Avengers movie.

Indeed, ever since that silly "Doomsday" chair casting announcement (in which most of the film's lead actors were revealed individually), fans have been expecting a superhero epic for the ages, with the MCU's first-ever star, Robert Downey Jr., returning to play the formidable villain Doctor Doom. The previous "Doomsday" trailers have emphasized the sheer menace of Doom (who's even got a whole bunch of towering Sentinels at his disposal), while reminding us that some of our faves, especially Thor (Chris Hemsworth) and Steve Rogers (Chris Evans), are returning to save the whole darn universe once again.

Knowing that "Avengers: Secret Wars" is a year away, moviegoers should expect a big ol' cliffhanger (and more than a couple of big character deaths) in "Doomsday." Does the film's new trailer offer any clues as to how this will all play out? Take a look above and see.

Okay folks, I don't want to rain on your parade, but is this doing it for anyone? Look, I know "Avengers: Doomsday" is going to be huge! A massive box office success! And I know fans will get a kick out of the fanservice on display here, like Cyclops saying the famous "To me, my X-Men!" line. But ... nothing here looks particularly interesting? Or new? There's a real "going through the motions" vibe to this footage. We've seen this before.

Industry observers note that it doesn't help that from a visual standpoint, "Doomsday" looks hideous. Every shot in this trailer has a drab, flat, lifeless appearance. Dare I say it, it looks ... boring? Come on, shouldn't we expect more at this point? Shouldn't we want more? Of course, who am I kidding? As I already noted, this is going to be huge. And to be fair, I'm sure the movie has more in store for us than what we're being shown in the trailer.

"Avengers: Doomsday" opens December 18, 2026.

Warning! Spoilers ahead for Season 9, Episode 7 of FBI, “Posterity,” streaming now with a Paramount+ subscription.

In a recent development, over the last few years, FBI has seen a surprising amount of cast changes in such a short amount of time. Just last season, the CBS procedural said goodbye to Emily Alabi not long after she joined the cast, and Juliana Aidén Martinez was then brought on. After a recent patch on the procedural pointed towards another exit on the 2026 TV schedule, I had to ask one star all about it, and they totally get why I have questions.

In a recent development, earlier in this season of FBI, John Boyd’s Stuart Scola revealed that wife and baby mama Nina Chase (Shantel VanSanten) had been offered the chance to lead her own task force in San Diego. Despite some hesitation, Scola ultimately tells her she should take it, and last week’s episode, “Posterity,” saw Nina getting ready for the big move. After some thinking, Scola told her he was going to put in a transfer to move to California with her, even if it would take a while.

It has been revealed that that development led me, and likely many fans, to worry that another exit could be coming and that we might say goodbye to Scola in the near future. However, Boyd told CinemaBlend what’s really going on and sought to ease concerns:.

In a recent development, I mean, look, as far as I know, there's no looks for any major changes, but I think that's a perfectly natural question to have. But really what's happening is exploring the character in a relationship in a very real way of something that we haven't yet tried with this couple, which real couples go through, all the time in life, which is career changes and geographics and movement. And what does it mean to love someone and let them go, ask them to stay, give up your thing?

Recent findings suggest that boyd's comments seem to point to the writers simply wanting to shake things up for Nina and Scola in a way they've never done before. The actor also told us this:.

According to recent reports, it's sacrifice and change, and it makes them super relatable. So, that's the story we're telling for now, but it's perfectly fine to kind of, hopefully, tease the idea of certain characters not being around anymore to see if people really love them.

I’m relieved to know that Boyd’s not going anywhere, at least not any time soon and that this is merely a chance to explore Scola and Nina’s relationship in a different way. When Nina was revealed to be moving to San Diego, there was no telling where things could be going for her and Scola, as well as their son, Dougie. And after the several cast exits the show has had in recent years, I appreciate the Boyd seems to understand why viewers would have questions.

Recent findings suggest that throughout the years, Nina and Scola have been through a lot, both as a couple and individually. While fans haven’t seen much of them since FBI: Most Wanted was canceled, we have been getting small updates here and there. Plus, VanSanten returned last season for the much-anticipated Scolina wedding. There's no telling how the relationship will progress, given they're working on opposite sides of the country and trying to raise their son together. I, for one, am eager to see how it plays out.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Also, even if there aren’t any plans to move Scola to San Diego in the near future, that isn’t stopping potential Scolina spinoff ideas. When asked by CinemaBlend if FBI could expand with another spinoff centered on Scola and Nina in San Diego, VanSanten remarked she was already campaigning for a fresh series. Unsurprisingly, Boyd reiterated his intention to stay with the Mothership. But, if we do eventually see Scola leaving 26 Fed, it would be fun to follow the fan-favorite couple in California.

In a recent development, I’m excited to see what FBI has planned for this next Scolina obstacle, and as long as Boyd is not leaving the series any time soon, I’ll be fine. All in all, fans should really stay tuned in as Season 9 continues. 💡 Key Takeaways

  • Léa Seydoux and Daniel Craig pose as they arrive on the set of No Time To Die on September 09, 2019 in Matera, Italy.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, since the beginning of the week, the James Bond frenzy has shown no signs of stopping. On November 16, newly introduced Bond owners Amazon MGM Studios finally revealed the name of the actor who will succeed Daniel Craig as 007: Robert Pattinson. After years of speculation and months of intense rumors, the next James Bond now has a new face. Now, the next question on everyone’s mind: Who will be the next Bond girl?

It has been revealed that the exception in thie great debate is Léa Seydoux. The actor, who seems to be everywhere this year, played Madeleine Swann in Craig's final Bond films, Spectre (2015) and No Time to Die (2021). Her magnetic performance made Madeleine an unforgettable Bond girl, especially since her character plays a decisive role in the arc of Craig’s character: at the end of No Time to Die, the famous spy sacrifices himself to save her and their daughter, Mathilde. For the first time since its creation in 1953 by British author Ian Fleming, the secret agent in Her Majesty’s service was gone.

Léa Seydoux and Daniel Craig pose as they arrive on the set of No Time To Die on September 09, 2019 in Matera, Italy.

In a recent interview on Vogue's The Run-Through podcast, Seydoux was candid about how little interest she had in her successor. “I don’t really care,” she mentioned with a laugh. “I don’t really care, guys. How can you?”.

When pressed on who Pattinson's female lead might be, Seydoux expressed mixed feelings about the British spy's latest iteration. With the purchase of the Bond IP by Amazon, “It became American," Seydoux said. “But I’m sure the movie will be great because it’s directed by Denis Villeneuve, who’s a very talented director. I’m sure he will do something great.”.

The online megamart took control of the storied franchise in 2023, after which Amazon founder Jeff Bezos controversially sought feedback on the title character's casting via X. The announcement of Villeneuve as the next film's director brought things back from the brink.

Bezos, who confirmed that he was “very involved” in the film's casting process, also seems to give Seydoux pause. In an interview with Variety, she admitted “was a bit sad when I heard that it was sold (…) but now that it’s Denis, I was like, Oh, at least it’s him, so it will be cinema.”.

Denis Villeneuve, who directed Seydoux in Dune: Part Two, will release the final installment of this epic science-fiction trilogy will be on December 16. After that, he'll be free to focus on his next major project: reviving the world’s most famous secret agent. It remains to be seen who he will choose to star opposite Robert Pattinson as his female companion—but we know that despite her fondness for the director, Seydoux will not return: Just last month, the French actress told People “I really loved being on this franchise, but now it’s ... done.”.

Industry News: A Doctor Doom And Doctor Strange Team-Up Is One Of The Best Marvel Comics Ever

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (909 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Slashfilm

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Doctor Victor von Doom is a master of magic, so little surprise he's often crossed paths with the Sorcerer Supreme, Doctor Stephen Strange.
  • Sources indicate that written by Roger Stern, one of the best writers in the 1980s Marvel Comics bullpen, and drawn by Mike Mignola, future creator of the "Hellboy" universe, "Triumph and Torment" is indeed a triumph.
  • Industry observers note that doom's usual nemeses, Reed Richards and the Fantastic Four, are nowhere to be seen.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Doctor Victor von Doom is a master of magic, so little surprise he's often crossed paths with the Sorcerer Supreme, Doctor Stephen Strange. Their first meeting, and the foundation for their mutual respect, was in 1989's "Doctor Strange and Doctor Doom: Triumph and Torment," one of the essential Doctor Doom comics every Marvel fan should read.

Sources indicate that written by Roger Stern, one of the best writers in the 1980s Marvel Comics bullpen, and drawn by Mike Mignola, future creator of the "Hellboy" universe, "Triumph and Torment" is indeed a triumph. It was published in the "Marvel Graphic Novel" line, itself designed to tell standalone and more mature stories featuring Marvel's character stable.

Industry observers note that doom's usual nemeses, Reed Richards and the Fantastic Four, are nowhere to be seen. While, conceptually, Doom needs Richards, tales like "Triumph and Torment" prove how he can hold individual stories without the FF. "Triumph and Torment" is also one of the most convincing arguments for Doom being more than a villain.

In Doom's debut, Stan Lee and Jack Kirby's "Fantastic Four" #5, it's established he had, during his and Reed's time at college, been obsessed with dark magic and built a machine to enter the nether world, which blew up and scarred him. His fuller origin in "Fantastic Four Annual" #2 revealed his ambition was to contact his mother, Cynthia von Doom, a witch who died during his childhood. Cynthia's trunk of magical secrets begat Victor's own knowledge of sorcery.

Sources indicate that A 1971 story in "Astonishing Tales" #8 (by Gerry Conway and Gene Colan) then revealed that every Midsummer's Eve (when the liminal walls between worlds are the thinnest), Doom battles the forces of Hell to free his mother's soul, only to reach a stalemate. So, in "Triumph and Torment," Doom does the unthinkable and asks for help.

Sources indicate that in "Triumph and Torment," both Strange and Doom partake in a contest of the world's greatest sorcerers held by Strange's god-like patrons, the Vishanti. Strange wins with Doom placing second — a familiar place for him, but it works in his favor. Per contest rules, Strange must grant a "boon" of Doom's choosing, and Doom wants Strange's assistance in freeing his mother's soul.

It has been revealed that "Is one woman's soul beneath the notice of the Sorcerer Supreme?" Doom asks a surprised Strange, who in turns questions why Doom never requested his help before. "I will bear any ordeal, Strange, but Doctor Doom does not beg," he replies. That pride is ultimately crucial to Doom's plan to free Cynthia.

In Hell, facing the overwhelming power of the demon lord Mephisto, Doom seemingly trades Strange's soul for his mother's. But Cynthia, a noble woman, refuses and spurns Victor — a sacrifice that secures her place in Heaven. Doom finally frees his mother and outwits her devilish captor. This plan both flatters and damns Doom's character. He values his mother's safety more than her love for him, but his own pride most of all.

According to recent reports, "Triumph and Torment" helps itself stand alone by exploring Doom and Strange's origins, so you can understand both men completely from this one story. Their journeys are also quite similar, as physical injuries prompt both men to venture high into the Himalayas seeking mystical knowledge. The book retells Cynthia's death, and Victor's childhood, via Doom's attendant Boris. Along with the reader, Strange realizes that beneath Doom's cold armor lies a child of tragedy. Upon taking his mask for the first time, Doom swears that pain and compassion are for lesser men — but his blueprint to free his mother, and what it costs him, prove otherwise.

Mike Mignola's art in "Triumph and Torment" makes Doctor Doom, his castle, and Latveria feel more truly gothic than in any other comic. Knowing Mignola went on to create a demonic superhero, too, it's hard not to compare "Triumph and Torment" to "Hellboy." Mignola drawing Strange and Doom facing down demons feels like a "Hellboy" test run in the same way his Batman comic "Sanctum" was.

In the documentary "Mike Mignola: Drawing Monsters," Mignola admitted he felt out of place drawing typical Marvel superhero books during the 1980s. "I'm not cut out to draw superheroes [...or] cars and buildings, most of the stuff that comics are made of," Mignola explained. He'd much rather be drawing monsters, which is why "Triumph and Torment" was a perfect assignment for him. Mignola's penciling especially comes to vibrant life once Doom and Strange enter Hell.

Far from looking identical, the demons all have different skin tones, weapons, and proportions. Some have wings, one is a humanoid torso on a giant serpent's tail, etc. Inker/colorist Mark Badger, rather than using a single background color for Hell, employs red-orange-yellow-green gradients. Mixed with Mignola's heavy shadows, it looks truly creepy, ethereal, and dangerous, like the typical fire and brimstone version of Hell but made even stranger. Compare this to the scary and lonely underworld in Mignola's 2010s series "Hellboy in Hell," and you can see an artist who grew.

Of course, the greatest achievement in "Triumph and Torment" is Doctor Doom's. In "Astonishing Tales" #8, Doom's goal to free his mother from eternal damnation is presented as a Sisyphean task he'll never achieve. Thinking he could break the laws of Hell is a sign of Doom's immense self-regard and ambition — and incredibly, he eventually did it.

According to recent reports, the newest Hunger Games movie, Sunrise on the Reaping, had a gigantic opening weekend that exceeded expectations. Some theorized it could struggle as people stayed home to playGTA 6, which released one day prior, but that doesn't appear to have been the case. At the domestic box office, Sunrise on the Reaping earned $120 million for its opening weekend, with $105 million more from international markets for a total of $225 million over its first three days, according to Deadline. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lYXtL5TreOE The franchise's second prequel, after 2023's The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes, Sunrise on the Reaping tells the story of the 50th Hunger Games, where Haymitch Abernathy emerged victorious. Joseph Zada plays him; Woody Harrelson played Haymitch in the original Hunger Games films. Sunrise on the Reaping also stars Ralph Fiennes as a younger President Snow, Jesse Plemons as a younger Plutarch, and Elle Fanning as a younger Effie. With $120 million for its domestic opening, Sunrise on the Reaping is now just the second prequel film ever to start with $100 million or more domestically. The current top prequel is 2016's Star Wars movie Rogue One, which made $155 million for its domestic opening. Some had theorized that Sunrise on the Reaping could suffer as people stayed home to play GTA 6 instead. Director Francis Lawrence mentioned, "Hopefully, people find time for both." It sure seems like he was right about that. For comparison, The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes debuted to just $44.6 million for its opening weekend in North America, so Sunrise on the Reaping is doing much better. Sunrise on the Reaping is also Lionsgate's biggest post-COVID movie and its first film that opened to $100 million or more since 2015's The Hunger Games: Mockingjay: Part 2 ($102.6 million).

Recent findings suggest that let’s start with a latest WWII movie. This one debuted in theaters (a rarity for a Netflix original movie), and received largely lukewarm reviews. But its theme of bravery and brotherhood on the front line of a devastating conflict should still resonate. And it incorporates a very vital football game, so it actually ties in with my second pick of the week, Netflix's NFL gameday.

On the eve of Thanksgiving, Netflix will be the place to watch the Packers vs. Rams. Both teams have identical records this season, so it could be a closely contested matchup. And if football isn’t for you, how about the return of a Netflix original drama that explores an even more cutthroat world than professional athletics: an upper-society clique in East Texas.

According to recent reports, these are just some of the movies and reveals heading to Netflix this week. Alongside my top picks, you’ll find a full schedule of everything new on Netflix over the next seven days. And for a complete overview, here’s a guide to everything new on Netflix in November 2026.

What it's about: In the wake of the devastating attack on Pearl Harbor, four young football players (Nicholas Galitzine, Bill Skarsgård, Ray Nicholson and Tom Francis) enlist in the Marine Corps. Ahead of the Battle of Okinawa, they participate in a football match that for just a moment lets the frontline soldiers forget the horrors soon to come.

Why you should watch it: “The Mosquito Bowl’s” focus on the brutality of WWII, camaraderie, and the sacrifices made by ordinary people — each member of the quartet effectively gives up their athletic dreams to enlist — is not latest for the genre, but they’re worthwhile topics, and this Netflix original should still be an emotionally impactful watch.

Watch "The Mosquito Bowl" starting November 25.

What it's about: Netflix’s push into live broadcasting continues with the first-ever Thanksgiving Eve live NFL game. The matchup will be held at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood between the Los Angeles Rams and the Green Bay Packers. So far this season, both teams are 6-4.

Sources indicate that why you should watch it: Thanksgiving and football are synonymous, so you probably don’t need convincing to watch a live NFL broadcast alongside your family over the holiday. Personally, as a Chargers fan (please feel free to mock me in the comments), I'm excited to enjoy this one as neutral, and I'll probably get to witness a higher standard of football as well.

It has been revealed that watch "NFL Netflix Gameday: Packers vs. Rams"live on November 25 (8:15 p.m. ET / 5:15 p.m. PT).

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A man is accused of killing his coworker with a crossbow at a Louisiana country club two days after a sheriff claims he strangled a woman to death along a nature trail out of “impulse.”.

It has been revealed that jared Schurr, of Mandeville, is facing two separate counts of second-degree murder in the unrelated killings of Lizeht Rodriguez and his former coworker and friend, Woodrow Scott, according to the St. Tammany Parish Sheriff’s Office.

Investigators first learned about the murder of Rodriguez, 24, on November 11, when a citizen alerted authorities to a body off of a trail at the Northlake Nature Center in Mandeville, St. Tammany Parish Sheriff Bret Ibert mentioned during a Monday, November 23, news conference.

An autopsy revealed she was fatally strangled along the nature trail, according to the sheriff.

As authorities investigated Rodriguez’s murder, Ibert said “on Friday the 13th, at 11:30 a.m., Woodrow Scott was brutally murdered in the Covington Country Club.”.

Schurr, 36, who’s accused of shooting Scott, 37, in the back with a crossbow, was identified as a suspect through license plate reader technology, according to the sheriff.

He was traced to Mississippi, where he was arrested and booked in the state’s Pearl River County Jail, the sheriff said.

Recent findings suggest that when St. Tammany Parish investigators visited Schurr in custody, he allegedly confessed to killing Scott.

Scott’s loved ones told Fox 8 Live that Schurr was a close friend, with Scott’s three daughters considering Schurr as family, according to his 11-year-old daughter, Kyndall Scott.

Sources indicate that “We would call him our uncle. We told him that we loved him,” Kyndall mentioned while speaking to the TV station.

Candice Metz, Scott’s ex-wife, told the TV station that Schurr suddenly shot Scott with a crossbow at a construction site at the Covington Country Club. Scott was reportedly laying down floor tiles at the time of the incident.

Ibert noted during the news conference that while Schurr “admitted to the murder of Mr. Scott, at no time did he indicate any involvement in the Rodriguez homicide.”.

In a recent development, detectives investigating Rodriguez’s murder with the help of the FBI searched a creek for evidence relating to her killing and also reviewed digital evidence from local cell towers, according to the sheriff. Evidence uncovered during the investigation pointed to Schurr as a suspect.

At a property Schurr had been renting, detectives executed a search warrant and discovered items connecting him to “the Rodriguez murder scene,” Ibert mentioned.

Afterward, detectives revisited Schurr in jail, where he allegedly confessed to killing Rodriguez.

Schurr was one of several people Rodriguez had passed at the Northlake Nature Center the day she was killed, Ibert mentioned.

Schurr told detectives he visited the park that day for the first time in more than 15 years, according to the sheriff.

He allegedly revealed he grabbed and fatally strangled Schurr in an “impulse” attack, the sheriff noted.

Afterward, Schurr allegedly dragged her body off the trail before she was discovered by another person, the sheriff’s office said in a statement.

“This investigation remains ongoing,” Ibert said.

It wasn’t clear whether Schurr had an attorney who could comment on his behalf at the time of publication.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that if you thought the wait to finally hear Chris Evans' Steve Rogers announce (well, more like theatrically whisper), "Avengers, assemble!" in 2019's "Avengers: Endgame" was long enough, then that's nothing compared to the plight of "X-Men" enthusiasts ever since the first 20th Century Fox film came out in 2000. Arguably no fanbase has suffered more in that time, enduring a steady stream of relatively comic book-y blockbusters that mostly just seemed embarrassed of their own source material, with only a few exceptions thrown into the mix. Whatever you might say about "Avengers: Doomsday" leading up to its release, however, "comic book-y" has to be at the top of the list — and the final "Doomsday" trailer has just given us the famous line every nerd has been dying to witness.

Yes, this is a perfect excuse to link to the memorable "Say the line, Bart!" gag from "The Simpsons." "X-Men" fans have read it in the comics, they've actually seen it before in the animated "X-Men: '97" series, and it basically seemed like a fait accompli that Marvel would find a way to deliver this moment in live action for "Doomsday." You know what we're talking about: Cyclops (James Marsden), leader of the mutant team of superheroes, finally bellowing out, "To me, my X-Men!".

In a recent development, the only wrinkle is probably the idea of dropping this reveal in a trailer, as opposed to saving it for the movie itself. Would it have been ideal to experience this for the very first time in theaters on opening weekend, rather than on your phone while walking into work on a Monday morning? Of course! Does that make the actual scene any less thrilling? Probably not! So, without further ado, let's overanalyze this to within an inch of its life below.

In a recent development, could anyone have imagined seeing this comic book panel come to life before their very eyes in "Avengers: Doomsday"? Okay, sure, the circumstances aren't exactly what most fans would've anticipated in a vacuum. Rather than seeing this moment occur after several successful "X-Men" movies spent years carefully laying the foundation for Scott Summers to become the leader of the team we know and love from the comics, this is getting shoehorned into a crossover movie pitting a few familiar "X-Men" film stars against a villain they have no real connection to in Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom. And despite the "X-Men"-centric nature of this call to action, it's at least a little funny to hear him specifically assemble his fellow mutants and then watch several members of the Avengers and Fantastic Four arrive in perfect formation.

But between the awfully long wait for this moment and James Marsden's delivery of this dialogue (which is pretty similar to the one in Season 1 of the widely well-received "X-Men '97"), it's tough to imagine many fans out there will feel inclined to nitpick anything. Directors Joe and Anthony Russo are clearly hoping this begins to set things right for a group of mutants who've deserved a much better live-action fate than they've typically received. So, while the internet spends the next few weeks arguing over whether this sequence had the requisite amount of hype and payoff to decades of build up, the rest of the moviegoing population has probably already been convinced to fork over approximately $2 billion for this latest "Avengers" extravaganza. So it goes!

The Avengers, X-Men, Fantastic Four, and more will arrive in "Avengers: Doomsday" on December 18, 2026.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, hailee Steinfeld just became a mama earlier this year when her and her husband Josh Allen welcomed their daughter in the spring. It was just confirmed that she’s got not one but two projects among upcoming 2026 movies – now that the final Avengers: Doomsday trailer showed Kate Bishop among the massive roster of heroes. But will her new starring role in her daughter’s life change how she approaches Hollywood going forward?

It has been revealed that most fresh mothers have to ask themselves the question of how work might change their lives once they become one. Here’s what Steinfeld stated about it when it was posed to her by Entertainment Tonight:.

I guess I’ve always made projects with the thought in my mind somewhere in there, maybe not necessarily at the front of it, but that like, I’ll get to share this with my family someday.

It has been revealed that the beginning of Steinfeld’s answer reminds me how she famously decided to explore her own mixed heritage roots when she got to play Mary in Sinners. The actress remarked that the research for that role was looking into her family history, and that brought her closer to her mother and her grandfather, who account for the Filipino and African American side of her ancestry. These days she’s going to also think of her daughter too when she picks jobs, too. As Steinfeld said herself:.

Industry observers note that and now, I do feel like maybe moving forward that’ll be something I strongly take into account. But, the fact that [Hexed] was the first thing that came into my life and the first project that she is really a part of is really special.

Recent findings suggest that steinfeld’s latest movie is Walt Disney Animation’s latest, Hexed, which is all about a mother and her teen daughter at its core against a backdrop of a world of witches. The 29-year-old has shared before that the role came at a time where a story about “an overprotective mother makes a hell of a lot more sense to me” than it would have before this phase of her life.

In the movie, Steinfeld plays Billie, a misfit teenager who finds out she’s been a witch her whole life, but that her powers have been concealed by her mom with a bracelet. Rashida Jones voices the role of her mother along with Jodie Foster playing an evil witch named Celeste and Walton Goggins playing a three-eyed cat named Beef Roger. Hexed has earned positive reactions ahead of its release this Wednesday, November 25.

In a recent development, outside of her latest role, Steinfeld is confirmed to reprise her role as Kate Bishop in Avengers: Doomsday, hitting theaters on December 18. Then we’ll hear her voice again as Gwen Stacy/Spider-Gwen in Spider-Man: Beyond the Spider-Verse coming out on June 18. We’re so curious what’s next for Steinfeld in her newly introduced mom era! For now, she’s staying booked and busy even as she enjoys some much-deserved time off with her baby daughter, Harper Haize Allen.
